The study included patients \ge18 years of age with a confirmed diagnosis of CAD based on the following criteria; chronic hemolysis, polyspecific direct antiglobulin test (DAT) positive, monospecific DAT strongly positive for C3d, cold agglutinin titer \ge64 at 4°C, and IgG DAT \le 1+.

endpoint.text: Composite responder rate: no blood transfusion from Week 5 through Week 26, no prohibited CAD medication, and Hgb >=12 g/dL or increase of >=2 g/dL from baseline at the treatment assessment timepoint

citations.quote: The primary efficacy endpoint was responder rate, which was a composite endpoint. A patient was considered a responder if he or she did not receive a blood transfusion from Week 5 through Week 26 (end of treatment) and did not receive treatment for CAD beyond what was permitted per protocol.
In addition, the patient's hemoglobin level at the assessment time point must have met either of the following criteria: Hgb level \ge 12 g/dL or Hgb level increased by \ge 2 g/dL from baseline.
The efficacy of ENJAYMO was assessed in an open-label, single-arm, 6-month trial in 24 patients (CARDINAL, NCT03347396).

result.text: 13 of 24 patients (54.2%, 95% CI 32.8, 74.4) met the composite responder criteria, with the lower bound of the 95% CI >30%; components: 15 (62.5%) met the Hgb endpoint, 17 (70.8%) transfusion-free Weeks 5-26, 22 (91.7%) received no prohibited CAD medications

citations.quote: In total, 13 out of the 24 patients [54.2%, 95% confidence interval (CI): 32.8, 74.4] in the full analysis set met the responder criteria for the composite primary endpoint and the lower bound of the 95% CI of the response rate was >30%. The results for each of the components of the composite endpoint were also persuasive: 15 (62.5%) patients met the Hgb endpoint, 17 (70.8%) were transfusion-free from Week 5 to 26, and 22 (91.7%) patients did not receive protocol prohibited CAD medications.

indication.text: ENJAYMO is indicated to decrease the need for red blood cell (RBC) transfusion due to hemolysis in adults with cold agglutinin disease (CAD).

citations.quote: ENJAYMO (sutimlimab-jome) is indicated to decrease the need for red blood cell (RBC) transfusion due to hemolysis in adults with cold agglutinin disease (CAD).

target_moa.text: Humanized IgG4 monoclonal antibody that inhibits the classical complement pathway by binding C1s, a serine protease that cleaves C4; inhibition at the level of C1s prevents complement deposition on RBCs, resulting in inhibition of hemolysis in CAD

citations.quote: Sutimlimab-jome is an immunoglobulin G (IgG), subclass 4 (IgG4) monoclonal antibody (mAb) that inhibits the classical complement pathway (CP) and specifically binds to complement protein component 1, s subcomponent (C1s), a serine protease which cleaves C4. Sutimlimab-jome does not inhibit the lectin and alternative pathways. Inhibition of the classical complement
pathway at the level of C1s prevents deposition of complement opsonins on the surface of RBCs, resulting in inhibition of hemolysis in patients with CAD.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (>=10%): respiratory tract infection, viral infection, diarrhea, dyspepsia, cough, arthralgia, arthritis, and peripheral edema. Serious infections (including encapsulated bacteria) reported in 17% (4/24); serious adverse reactions in 13% (3/24). Infusion-related reactions in 2 of 24 patients (8%).

citations.quote: Most common adverse reactions (incidence \ge10%) are respiratory tract infection, viral infection, diarrhea, dyspepsia, cough, arthralgia, arthritis, and peripheral edema. (6.1)

Serious infections (bacterial and viral) were reported in 17% (4/24) of patients receiving ENJAYMO in a single-arm open-label clinical trial. These infections included sepsis, respiratory, and skin infections [see *Adverse Reactions* (6.1)].
Serious adverse reactions were reported in 13% (3/24) of patients who received ENJAYMO.
In the CARDINAL study, 2 of 24 patients (8%) treated with ENJAYMO experienced infusion-related reactions (shortness of breath, rapid heartbeat, nausea, flushing, and headache)
